The shape is deliberately thin, and every field it does NOT have is the point:

- **No renderer, no code.** A mode names existing sections. It cannot draw a row,
  which is why it needs no grants and cannot be a carriage channel — the worst a
  hostile mode can do is offer a tab list the user does not want, one menu row
  away from being switched off.
- **No row style.** How a section's rows draw belongs to that SECTION
  (`SidebarSectionSpec.rowStyle` in `@ryu/app-host/views`), because it is a
  property of the feed, not of an arrangement: a roster of named bots wants
  avatars whether or not the user is in a mode that features it. Putting it here
  would also mean a mode reaching across into another contribution's rendering,
  which is the coupling this member exists to avoid.
- **No `hidden` list.** A mode is a positive statement about what to show. The
  sections it does not name are simply not tabs in it.

Section ids are the shell's own keys (`agents`, `chats`, `spaces`, …) or another
contributed section's namespaced key (`plugin:<pluginId>:<sectionId>`). A named
section that does not resolve is dropped rather than failing the mode — an app
may legitimately name a section from a sibling app the user has not installed,
and losing one tab is a better answer than losing the mode.

default_section.description:
Which of `sections` the mode opens on. Absent (or naming a section not in
`sections`) = the first one. This is the field that makes a mode an opinion
rather than a filter: the shell's own Bot mode lists Sessions first but
opens on Agents, because the roster is what the mode is for.

description.description: One-line description shown under the title where the mode is offered.

icon.description: Optional glyph id resolved by the shell's Icon primitive (Iconify/Hugeicons).

id.description:
Stable id for this mode within the plugin (namespaced by the shell into the
stored mode key as `plugin:<pluginId>:<id>`, so two apps can both ship a
`bots` mode).

order.description: Optional ordering hint among the modes on offer (lower = earlier).

sections.description:
The sections this mode offers as tabs, in display order. Empty = the mode is
inert and the shell ignores it; a mode with one entry is a legitimate
single-surface arrangement, not an error.

title.description: Label shown in the sidebar's mode menu and the Appearance tab.

SidebarSectionContribution.description:
One app-registered **sidebar section** — a header plus a live list of rows the
desktop's compact sidebar renderer draws (the app-owned replacement for the
hardcoded Canvas/Whiteboard/Meetings sections). A typed envelope around an opaque
`spec` (the `SidebarSectionSpec` in `@ryu/app-host/views`: a `ViewSource` for the
rows, an `itemTarget` route template for `openTab`, optional `itemActions` and a
`create` action). Core stores it verbatim and tags it with the owning `plugin` id;
the `spec` stays opaque so a new section capability is a renderer change, not a
Core change.

icon.description: Optional glyph id resolved by the shell's Icon primitive (Iconify/Hugeicons).

id.description:
Stable id for this section within the plugin (namespaced into the shell's
section key as `plugin:<pluginId>:<id>`).

order.description: Optional placement hint among the sidebar sections (lower = higher up).

spec.description:
The opaque section spec (source/itemTarget/itemActions/create). Interpreted by
the desktop renderer, never by Core. Absent = a header with no rows.

title.description: Header label shown in the sidebar and the Customize dialog.

SidecarSpec.description: One managed sidecar process. The nested process/http/host_api payloads are intentionally left open here — they are large, evolve fastest, and the generated contract at crates/core/kernel-contracts/schemas/plugin-manifest.schema.json is their authority. This def pins the parts an author gets wrong most.

name.description: Local name, unique within the plugin. Namespaced to <plugin_id>/<name> by Core, and the key provides.sidecar references.

process.description: How Core obtains and runs the process. Tagged by kind so a future runtime is a data change, not a code change.

kind.description: binary: a checksum-verified download placed in the plugin's bin/ dir. python: the external-runtime provisioner (venv + pip + assets), then python -m <entry>. local: an already-present command on PATH or resolved from an env var. node: a bundled JS entrypoint.

port.description: TCP port the process's HTTP server binds to; used to build the health-check URL and the proxy target.

health_path.description: Health-check path on the process's server.

lazy.description: Spawn on first use instead of at plugin-enable.

idle_stop_secs.description: Scale-to-zero timeout in seconds: stop the sidecar after this long with no traffic. Absent means it stays up.

http.description: Optional HTTP proxy declaration. public_mount is the generic ext-proxy surface clients reach at /api/ext/<plugin_id>/… — the reason an app never needs a bespoke route baked into Core.

host_api.description: Optional host-API declaration: the subset of the owning plugin's approved grants this sidecar may call back into Core with.

provides_provider.description: Optional model-provider declaration, for a sidecar that serves an OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint Core should register as a provider.

sandbox.description: Optional OS-isolation declaration. The node operator chooses the isolation mode (off by default); this block can only make the sidecar stricter and declare the extra paths it needs beyond its own data directory and the temp directory.

mode.description: Minimum isolation mode this sidecar asks for. Combined with the node setting by taking the stricter of the two.

fs.description: Extra filesystem paths. Each starts with $APP_DATA, $TMP, $RYU_DIR/<entry>, or $HOME/<entry>; '..', '.', empty segments, backslashes, ':', and other apps' directories are rejected.

read.description: Paths the sidecar may read and execute from.

write.description: Paths the sidecar may read and write.

memory_limit_mb.description: Memory cap for the sidecar's process tree in MiB. Applied on Windows only.

StoreTabContribution.description:
One app-registered **marketplace tab** — a section in the Store's nav bar whose
content is the app's own installable catalog. A typed envelope around an opaque
`spec` (the `StoreTabSpec` in `@ryu/app-host/views`: a `ViewSource` for the rows,
a `groupBy`/`groups` split into card sections, an `install` action, and per-item
actions). Core stores it verbatim and tags it with the owning `plugin` id; the
`spec` stays opaque so a new catalog capability is a renderer change, not a Core
change.

**There is no first-party escape hatch.** This contribution used to carry a
`view` naming a hand-written renderer the shell kept in a plugin-id allowlist,
for the one tab whose detail pane the vocabulary could not express (the
workflow-template graph). That made the flagship example of "an app can own a
Store section" the single section no other app could reproduce. The graph is a
declarative primitive now (`spec.detail.graph`), the field is gone, and every
contributed tab — first-party or not — renders from the same spec.

group.description:
Which nav cluster the pill joins — the shell draws a divider wherever the
group changes. Built-in groups: `discover`, `catalog`, `community`, `manage`,
`account`. An unknown value gets its own cluster rather than being dropped.

icon.description: Optional glyph id resolved by the shell's Icon primitive (Iconify/Hugeicons).

id.description:
Stable id for this tab within the plugin. The shell namespaces it into the
section key as `plugin:<pluginId>:<id>` so two apps can both ship a
`templates` tab.

order.description: Placement hint within the group (lower = further left).

spec.description:
The opaque tab spec (source/map/groups/search/install/itemActions). Interpreted
by the desktop renderer, never by Core. Absent alongside an absent `view` = an
empty tab.

subtitle.description: One-line description shown under the title in the section header.

Surface.description: A host surface the plugin can run on.

ThemeContribution.description:
One colour theme a plugin contributes (`contributes.themes`).

Shape-identical to the shell's own `ThemeVariant` (`@ryu/ui/theme/presets`), so a
theme installed from the marketplace and a theme that ships in the binary are the
same object by the time the picker renders them — there is no second rendering
path to keep in sync, and a plugin can never express a theme the built-ins could
not.

# Why `tokens` is an untyped map

The keys are CSS custom properties (`--background`, `--sidebar-ring`, …). Typing
them as a fixed struct would mean every new token added to the design system
silently DROPS out of third-party themes until Core is rebuilt and redeployed —
exactly the drift `settings_tabs` documents for its own `serde_json::Value`. The
values are never evaluated, only assigned to CSS variables, so an unknown key is
inert rather than dangerous.

id.description:
Stable id used as the persisted preset selection. Namespace it with the
plugin id (e.g. `"@acme/themes:midnight"`) so two plugins cannot collide, and
so a selection survives the theme being renamed.

label.description: Human name shown in the theme picker.

mode.description:
Which mode slot this theme fills: `"light"` or `"dark"`. A plugin shipping a
pair contributes two entries, mirroring how the shell keeps an independent
preset per mode rather than one theme with two halves.

preview.description: The four swatch colours the picker paints before the theme is applied.

ThemePreview.description: The swatch a theme shows in the picker, without applying the theme.

ToolFilterContribution.description: One tool id withheld from the model's offered tool list.

tool.description: Fully-qualified tool id (<server>.<tool>, e.g. browser.navigate), optionally ending in * to hide every tool with that prefix (shadow.* hides a whole server). The namespace is mandatory — a bare navigate is ambiguous across servers and is rejected at import. A trailing * is the only wildcard position allowed: an interior or leading * invites a pattern that silently matches far more than the author pictured.

reason.description: Why the plugin hides it. Surfaced in the plugin's listing so a user can see what a plugin removes from the model's view before installing it.

TurnHookContribution.description: One server-side chat turn hook. The body is a JS fragment run in the plugin sandbox with `ctx` (the turn context) and `host` (the capability bridge: host.sideModel, host.storage, host.log) in scope; it returns a directive such as {kind:"none"}, {kind:"note",text} or {kind:"continue",text}. Declare the body EITHER as `code_file` (recommended: a path to a real .js file you can read, lint and diff) OR inline as `code` — exactly one, never both.

id.description: Stable id for this hook (used in logging/audit), unique within the plugin.

on.description: The hook boundary this hook fires on. EITHER one of Core's built-in phases (the enum below) OR an app event declared by some installed plugin in its `contributes.hook_events`, written fully-qualified as `<owning plugin id>#<event name>` (e.g. `@ryu/meetings#meeting.ended`). Core dispatches by exact string match, so a phase spelled any other way is a hook that never runs. `stop` is an accepted alias of `post_assistant_turn` (Claude's naming). post_tool_use, subagent_stop, session_end, notification, model_select, session_tree, delegation_lifecycle and the three workflow_run_* phases are observation-only: their directives are not applied. action fires out of band for each normalized thinking or tool-call action in the assistant stream; it can never block or rewrite the stream, and only a `{kind:"note",text}` or `{kind:"tool_approval",question,summary}` directive is surfaced (as an action summary). pre_model_select fires after the agent binding resolves and before a model transport opens, and is the one awaited phase that may select a per-turn model. view_action runs only the owning plugin's hooks for a declarative view intent and, like an app event, honours only `{kind:"none"}` and `{kind:"note",text}`. plugin_update runs only the updated plugin's own hooks, from its new manifest, after a version change (update or rollback) so it can migrate its storage; it does not fire for a plugin that is disabled at the time, and likewise honours only `{kind:"none"}` and `{kind:"note",text}`. The workflow_run_* phases fire once per run as a user understands it — not per resume and not per nested sub-workflow — and a run suspended at an approval gate fires neither finished nor failed until it resumes and terminates. An app-event hook is likewise restricted to `{kind:"none"}` and `{kind:"note",text}` — it fires with no turn in flight, so `continue`/`replace`/`inject` have nothing to act on and are dropped. Subscribing to an event no installed plugin declares is allowed and simply never fires, so a consumer may be installed before its provider.

oneOf.description: An app event: `<owning plugin id>#<event name>`. The id half may be scoped (`@ryu/meetings`) or a legacy flat id.

code.description: The JS hook body inline. This is the WIRE form: `ryu pack` produces it by reading `code_file`, which is what keeps the whole body inside the Gateway-signed surface. Writing it by hand still works, but prefer `code_file` — a multi-kilobyte \n-escaped JSON string is not reviewable, and unreviewable code is where malicious behaviour hides.

code_file.description: Path to the file holding the hook body, relative to the plugin root, e.g. "hooks/review.js". Must be exactly `hooks/<name>.js` (or .mjs) — one directory deep, no traversal. The file is a FRAGMENT, not an ES module: Core splices it into an async IIFE, so a top-level `return` is correct and an `export` is not. Core resolves it at load time; `ryu pack` inlines it into `code` when bundling.

match.description: Optional cheap pre-gate, evaluated in Rust before the sandbox is spawned. Absent (or all fields empty) means the hook always runs.

ViewContribution.description:
One **declarative view** contribution (the Raycast tier — see `Contributes::views`).

A typed envelope around an opaque `spec`: Core stores it verbatim, tags it with
the owning `plugin` id at `GET /api/plugins/contributions`, and forwards it to the
surface shell, which maps `view` + `spec` to native components. The `spec` shape is
owned by the shared TS vocabulary (`@ryu/app-host/views`), NOT by this contract, so
adding a view kind is a renderer change, never a Core change.

id.description: Stable id for this view within the plugin (route/anchor key, unique per plugin).

spec.description:
The DATA payload for the view (items/columns/actions/fields/…). Opaque to Core
— the shared renderer interprets it per the `view` kind. Absent = an empty view.

title.description:
Optional human-facing title (tab label / palette entry). Absent = the shell
derives one from the view kind or the plugin name.

view.description:
The vocabulary member this view renders as — the discriminant the per-surface
renderer switches on (`"list-detail"`, `"data-table"`, `"form"`,
`"action-panel"`, `"filter-bar"`, `"empty-state"`, `"stat-card-row"`). Opaque
to Core; an unknown kind is passed through so a newer shell can render it.

WidgetContribution.description:
One app-widget contribution (Ryu Apps). Binds the tool that renders the widget
to its HTML template. `ui_entry` is the source entry the SDK `ryu pack` builds
into the self-contained HTML for third-party apps; built-in apps serve HTML
from the in-process provider and leave it unset.

tool_id.description: The fully-qualified tool id whose result renders this widget.
